weather_line: Fog holds in the hollows · porch railing watching the fog back

stories.section: Front Page · Platform Nine and Three-Quarters
stories.headline: First of September Arrives; Hogwarts Express Departs on Schedule; Wizarding World Pauses Briefly to Remember What It Was Like
stories.byline: By our heritage and sentiment correspondent
body: At precisely eleven o'clock this morning, the Hogwarts Express departed Platform Nine and Three-Quarters in a billow of steam that the assembled crowd agreed was, if anything, slightly more dramatic than strictly necessary. Trolleys were abandoned. Owls were startled. One grandmother waved at the wrong child for forty seconds before being gently corrected.

Senior Gringotts Liaison Christine, observing the occasion from her place of work — which is to say, from her desk, where the date has not escaped her notice — was seen to pause over a quarterly ledger for a full six seconds. The goblins observed the pause. No one said anything. It was agreed, wordlessly and professionally, that the first of September is allowed to mean what it means.

The Express arrived at Hogsmeade Station this afternoon precisely on time, which the Ministry has described as 'an annual exception we have decided to stop questioning.' Students are advised that the Forbidden Forest is still forbidden. The Ministry notes this every year. The forest has not commented.

stories.section: Home & Grounds · The Porch Railing Situation
stories.headline: Porch Railing Creaks Once at Dusk; Steve Considers This a Statement; Adam Consulted by Floo; Don's Portrait Volunteers Information About the Original Installation That Is Immediately Helpful and Immediately Regretted
body: The porch railing in question — third section, northeast corner, which Steve has been monitoring for forty-eight hours at a rate of approximately seven glances per daylight hour — issued a single, deliberate creak at seventeen minutes past six this evening. There was no wind. Steve noted this in a separate log.

Adam was consulted by Floo at half seven. Adam agreed that a creak with no wind was 'a thing.' He has offered to come and look at it, 'probably Saturday, depending.' Steve has entered this into the household schedule under 'Structural Reinforcements (Pending Brotherhood Confirmation).'

Don's portrait, which has been observing the situation from the hallway with the particular expression of a man who installed something in 1987 and is not prepared to say what he used, offered this evening that 'the northeast corner always had a bit of character.' He then added that he had shimmed it with a piece of a cabinet door and that the cabinet door had been a very good cabinet door. Christine has updated the household ledger. The railing has not creaked again. It does not need to.

stories.headline: Tuesday Brings Gringotts a Client Who Disputes an Eleven-Year-Old Transaction; Christine Resolves It; the Goblin Who Filed the Original Paperwork Has Not Been Told Yet; He Will Be Fine
body: A witch presented herself at the Gringotts Client Liaison desk this morning bearing a handwritten grievance regarding a vault transaction dated November of 2014, which she described as 'wrong, obviously wrong, and wrong in a way that has been bothering me since November of 2014.' Senior Liaison Christine received the grievance, the accompanying eleven years of compound indignation, and a folder of supporting documents that had been organised, the witch acknowledged, 'only this weekend.'

The matter was resolved in thirty-seven minutes. The original transaction had been mis-coded at entry. Christine located the error, cross-referenced three vault ledgers, produced the corrected figure, and had a goblin countersign the amendment before the client had finished her tea. The client expressed satisfaction. The goblins expressed the goblin equivalent of satisfaction, which is a very controlled absence of dissatisfaction.

The goblin who filed the original 2014 paperwork is currently on vault rotation in Sub-Corridor Fourteen and has not been informed. The Head Liaison has noted that he will be 'told appropriately, at an appropriate time, by the appropriate person.' Christine has been asked if she would like to be that person. She has said she will consider it.

stories.headline: The Gorge Acknowledges September; the Fog Adjusts Accordingly; the Eleven Ducks Are Noted to Have Adopted a More Autumnal Bearing
stories.byline: By our highland and hollow correspondent
body: The Red River Gorge issued its September acknowledgement at first light this morning, the fog descending two feet lower in the hollows than it has managed since April and arranging itself along the ridgeline with what observers have called 'intentional seasonal atmosphere.' The gorge does this every year. It has not been less impressive for the repetition.

The Jeep's eleven rubber ducks — presided over, as ever, by the deerstalker duck of the northeast corner — were observed this morning in what the Expedition Desk can only describe as an autumnal posture. The tam duck has been angled three degrees further into the wind. No one has touched them. The Jeep has not been moved. These things happen.

familiars_corner: Lucy: The household ledger has gained two new entries this week, which Lucy has reviewed and found adequately worded. She has added a third entry by unknown means. It concerns the biscuit shelf. It recommends no structural changes.

Ellie: Ellie observed the Hogwarts Express departing on the wireless broadcast this morning and became briefly, sincerely convinced that a very large dog was living inside the speaker. She has been sitting beside the speaker since half eleven. The speaker has not confirmed or denied this.

Jersey: September has arrived and with it, Jersey notes, a more compelling argument for the blanket. He has begun the blanket season unilaterally and without consultation. The household has ratified this decision retroactively.
founding_editor_note: The cabinet door was a perfectly good cabinet door, and I stand by it. Also, happy September. — D.

in_brief.sport: The Holyhead Harpies have announced their autumn training schedule; the team's bench-press totals were, per club custom, not disclosed, though a Gringotts source confirms the vault activity was 'impressively routine.'
in_brief.forecast: September fog, present and accounted for; the northeast porch corner watching the treeline; biscuit shelf secure, for now.

storyline_updates.title: The Porch Railing Situation
storyline_updates.summary: Day 2: The railing creaked once at dusk with no wind. Steve has logged it. Adam was consulted by Floo and has offered to come Saturday, pending. Don's portrait revealed the northeast corner was shimmed with a piece of a cabinet door, which he stands by. Christine has updated the household ledger. The railing has not creaked again. Day 3 should bring Adam's visit, or a further escalation — perhaps the railing does something more definitive (a second creak in response to a question, Steve and Adam's initial inspection, or Don's portrait producing a diagram of the original construction that raises more questions than it answers).
